sicilian.short_description: Black's most-analysed answer to 1.e4, fighting for an asymmetric game from move one.

french.short_description: Solid and structural — Black accepts a cramped position for a fixed pawn chain and counterplay on the queenside.

caro-kann.short_description: A reputation for solidity at any level — Black supports …d5 with …c6 and aims for a clean structure.

pirc-modern.short_description: Hypermodern systems where Black fianchettos and concedes the centre, then strikes back.

scandinavian.short_description: 1…d5 immediately challenges the centre — direct and easy to learn at club level.

alekhine.short_description: Provocative — Black invites White to chase the knight and overextend.

ruy-lopez.short_description: The classical 1.e4 main line — deep theory, slow strategic battles.

italian.short_description: The oldest open game — quiet Giuoco Pianissimo or sharp Evans Gambit.

scotch.short_description: White trades central tension for an open game and quick development.

kings-gambit.short_description: Romantic and aggressive — White sacrifices a pawn for the centre and the f-file.

vienna.short_description: A flexible 1.e4 e5 system that often transposes into King's Gambit positions.

petroff.short_description: Symmetrical and rock-solid — Black mirrors White and aims for equality.

philidor.short_description: An old, passive-but-solid setup with …d6 and …Nf6.

queens-gambit.short_description: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 — strategic battles around the central pawn structure.

slav.short_description: Black supports …d5 with …c6 and avoids the typical Queen's Gambit problems with the c8 bishop.

kings-indian.short_description: Black fianchettos the king's bishop, lets White claim the centre, then breaks with …e5 or …c5.

nimzo-indian.short_description: 3…Bb4 pins the c3-knight — flexible and structurally rich.

queens-indian.short_description: Black fianchettos to b7 and contests the long diagonal.

grunfeld.short_description: Black gives up the centre temporarily, then dismantles it with active piece play.

catalan.short_description: Queen's Gambit with a kingside fianchetto — long-term pressure on the long diagonal.

english.short_description: 1.c4 — flexible, transpositional, often reaches reversed Sicilian structures.

reti.short_description: A hypermodern start — White develops without committing the central pawns.

london.short_description: A solid, low-theory setup — White plays d4, Nf3, Bf4 in almost any move order.

kia.short_description: King's Indian setup with colours reversed — system-style with kingside attacking ideas.

dutch.short_description: 1…f5 — Black takes space on the kingside and plays for an attack.

benoni-benko.short_description: Asymmetric pawn structures — Benoni's central pawn chain or Benko's pawn sacrifice for queenside pressure.

trompowsky.short_description: An early Bg5 sidesteps the Indian defenses and provokes structural concessions.

irregular.short_description: Off-beat first moves — gambits and surprises rarely seen at master level.
